Diagram for set-up. [1A]

Connect the long wire to the galvanometer/connect the apparatus as shown. [1A]

Put/place/move the wire across the magnetic field between the pair of magnets. [1A]

Any TWO of the following investigations, at 2A each; total 7 marks.

Relative movement: move the wire vertically down across the field and then up; the galvanometer light spot deflects to one side and then to the opposite side.

Polarities of magnet: move the wire vertically down across the field and observe the deflection. Reverse the magnet polarities and repeat; the galvanometer deflects to the opposite side.

Direction of movement: moving the wire vertically up/down across the field gives a large deflection. No deflection occurs when it is moved horizontally to the left/right in the field instead.

Orientation of conductor: with the wire perpendicular to the magnetic field, move it vertically up/down across the field; the galvanometer gives a large deflection. No deflection occurs when the wire is placed parallel to the field instead.

Rate of movement: move the wire slowly across the field and then quickly; the galvanometer deflects more for a quicker movement/faster rate.

Number of turns: wind the wire into, say, a 10-turn coil and move it across the field again; more turns give a greater galvanometer deflection.

(a) Write a nuclear equation for the decay. (2 marks)

*(b) Given: mass of a radium nucleus = 226.0254 u

Calculate the energy released in the decay in MeV. (2 marks)

(c) 1 curie (Ci) is defined as the activity of 1 g of radium. The activity of a radium source used in laboratories is about 5 μCi. Estimate the number of radium atoms in this source and hence find its activity expressed in disintegrations per second. The half-life of radium-226 is 1600 years and take the mass of one mole of radium as 226 g. (1 μCi = 1×10−6 Ci) (3 marks)

(a) Ra88226 → Rn86222 + He24 (He / α). [2A]

(b) Δm = 226.0254−(222.0176+4.0026) = 0.0052 u. [1M]

Energy released = (0.0052)(931) = 4.84 MeV. [1A; total 2]

(c) Number of radium atoms: N = NA(1/226)(5×10−6) = (6.02×1023)(1/226)(5×10−6) = 1.33×1016. [1A]

Activity A = (ln 2 / t½)N = [ln 2/(1600×365×24×3600)](1.33×1016). [1M]

A = 1.83×105 disintegrations per second (Bq). [1A; total 3]
2012|paper-1b|11.reasoning:
(a) An α-particle carries mass number 4 and atomic number 2. Conserve both totals: 226 = 222+4 and 88 = 86+2, giving radon-222 and a helium-4 nucleus.

(b) Use the given nuclear masses consistently. The positive mass loss is 0.0052 u; 1 u c² = 931 MeV gives 4.84 MeV. This is the total released energy, not necessarily the kinetic energy of the α-particle alone because the daughter nucleus recoils.

(c) For the same isotope, activity is proportional to atom number and mass. Under the question’s definition, 5 μCi corresponds to 5×10−6 g of radium. Divide by 226 g mol−1 and multiply by NA to obtain 1.33×1016 atoms.

Then apply A = λN with λ = ln 2 / T½. Convert 1600 years to seconds first (5.04576×1010 s); this gives about 1.83×105 Bq. Do not treat μCi as a mass unit without first using the definition in the question.
